 Mr. Vivek Goyal, Advocate for the petitioner
 Ms. Ambika Luthra, Additional Advocate General, Haryana
 *

**
Jagmohan Bansal, J. (Oral)
1.

The petitioner through instant petition under Articles 226/227 of the Constitution of India is
seeking setting aside of order whereby he was dismissed from service.

2.  The petitioner was dismissed from service on account of his implication in FIR No.828 dated 08.09.2022 under Sections 323, 342, 354-D, 376, 376(2)(n) and 506 of Indian Penal Code, 1860 registered at Police Station Shahabad, Kurukshetra.
A regular departmental inquiry was initiated against him and vide order dated 26.12.2022 he was suspended.
He was held guilty in departmental inquiry and was awarded punishment of dismissal from service for his misconduct.
He unsuccessfully preferred appeal and his revision before Director General of Police is still pending.
He faced trial and came to be acquitted by Trial Court vide judgment dated 05.09.2025.
He requested Director General of Police, Haryana to reinstate him in service in the light of his acquittal in aforesaid criminal case but to no avail.
1 of 2

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that as per Rule 16.3 of Punjab Police Rules, 1934 (as applicable to State of Haryana) (for short 'PPR'), the case of petitioner needs to be reconsidered.

4. On being confronted with judgment dated 02.04.2025 passed by this Court in CWP No.18777 of 2023, Bala Singh v. State of Haryana and Others; judgment dated 21.05.2025 passed in CWP No.21304 of 2024 Nirmaljit Singh v. State of Punjab and Others; and judgment dated 27.05.2025 passed in CWP No.25411 of 2022, Dheeraj Kumar v. State of Haryana and Others, Ms. Ambika Vikash vs State Of Haryana And Others on 2 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153590074/
1 Luthra, Additional Advocate General, Haryana, expressed her inability to controvert the fact that matter needs to be considered as per Rule 16.3 of PPR.
5.

sentences.text: In the light of orders passed in Bala Singh (Supra), Nirmaljit Singh (Supra) and Dheeraj Kumar (Supra) as well as Rule 16.3 of PPR, the Revisionary Authority is directed to adjudicate revision within two months from today, keeping in mind Rule 16.3 of PPR and judgment of acquittal.
6. Disposed of in above terms.
7. It is made clear that nothing observed hereinabove shall be construed as expression of opinion of this Court on merits of the case.

(JAGMOHAN BANSAL)
